documents.summary: A legal-affairs page of suggested syllabus language. Its AI section tells faculty to state when AI may be used and gives two optional policies (permit everywhere with attribution, or only on designated assignments with attribution), plus guidance on AI-detection tools and student consent.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule; it says faculty "should notify students how and when generative AI tools" may be used and offers "two suggested syllabus policies ... depending on the level of generative AI use the faculty member wants to permit". It hands the decision to instructors and lists two tiers, so delegates.

notes: Scope: all four included documents are university-layer and aimed at faculty or employees; no college or computing unit policy exists. Syllabus page is mostly unrelated syllabus boilerplate; only the AI section, AI-detection notice and consent rules were coded. Option 2 repeats Option 1's disclosure and data-protection text; those exact repeats were not coded again. General syllabus lines (violation penalties, proof assignments are own work, recording bans) were skipped as not AI-specific. FAQ and syllabus page say detectors should not be relied on, yet the syllabus page supplies template language for detector use with consent. Candidate new types: mentor/supervisor approval before AI use (OUR); consent and notice before detector use (syllabus page).
